metaTitle: BMW Oil Leak & Gasket Repair | BMW Garage
metaDescription: Professional oil leak and gasket repair for all BMW models. Valve cover, oil filter housing, oil pan, rear main seal, and turbo oil line repairs. Free inspection & fixed quotes.

blocks.html: We carry out full oil leak repairs on BMW engines, addressing leaks from gaskets, seals, and mating surfaces. Our process ensures the leak is permanently sealed without damaging surrounding components.

items: **Leak identification** – we use UV dye and thorough cleaning to pinpoint the exact source.
**Access & disassembly** – components are carefully removed to reach the leaking gasket or seal.
**Surface preparation** – mating surfaces are cleaned and prepared to OEM standards, especially critical on aluminium blocks.
**Gasket/seal replacement** – all old gaskets and seals are replaced with genuine or high-quality equivalents.
**Reassembly & torqueing** – all fasteners are torqued to BMW specifications to prevent future leaks.
**Final testing** – the engine is run and inspected for any remaining leakage.

blocks.html: We cover all common BMW leak points, including valve cover gaskets, oil filter housing gaskets, oil pan gaskets, rear main seals, VANOS solenoid seals, and turbo oil lines (especially on N63 and S63 V8 engines).

paras: Oil leak repairs vary depending on the source and labour involved. We provide a fixed-price quote after a full inspection. Call us or use the registration lookup for an initial estimate.

blocks.html: Oil leaks can occur on any BMW engine, but certain models and engine families are more prone. We perform leak repairs across the entire BMW range, with particular expertise on:
E60, F10, G30 – common on N63, N57, and N55.
E70, F15, G05 – N63 and N57 oil leaks are frequent.
Same engine families as X5 – N63, N57, B57.
E9x (S65) and F80 (S55) – rod bearings aside, oil leaks from valve covers and oil filter housing.
F10 (S63) – hot-vee turbo oil lines and valve seals are common.
For variant-specific guidance, see our [330i](/bmw-330i-engines), [530i](/bmw-530i-engines), [X5 xDrive50i](/bmw-x5-xdrive50i-engines), and [M5](/bmw-m5-engines) engine pages.

sections.heading: Our Process for Oil Leak Repair

steps.title: Inspection & Diagnosis
steps.body: We perform a visual inspection, clean the engine, and apply UV dye to trace the exact leak source.

steps.title: Access & Disassembly
steps.body: Components obstructing the leak are removed – this may involve lifting the engine or lowering subframes.

steps.title: Surface Preparation
steps.body: Mating surfaces are cleaned and prepared to ensure a perfect seal – especially critical on aluminium blocks.

steps.title: Gasket & Seal Replacement
steps.body: All old gaskets and seals are replaced with genuine or high-quality equivalents.

steps.title: Reassembly & Torqueing
steps.body: Components are refitted and all fasteners are torqued to BMW specifications.

steps.title: Testing & Final Check
steps.body: We run the engine, check for leaks, and road-test if necessary.

items.q: How do I know if my BMW has an oil leak?
items.a: Common signs include oil spots under the car, burning oil smell, low oil level warnings, or visible oil residue on the engine. We recommend a professional inspection.

items.q: How long does an oil leak repair take?
items.a: It depends on the leak location. Valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets can take 2–4 hours; oil pan and rear main seal jobs may take a full day due to subframe or engine removal.

items.q: Can you repair oil leaks on all BMW models?
items.a: Yes, we work on all BMW models from the 1 Series to the X7 and M-cars, including all engine types – petrol, diesel, and performance variants.

items.q: Do you use genuine BMW parts?
items.a: We use genuine BMW parts or OEM-equivalent quality, depending on availability and customer preference.
Yes, every repair comes with a 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.
